title: Feature Go-To-Market Playbook: Dashboards, Rollouts, and Cost Transparency Enablement
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic GTM playbook and coordination checklist for the upcoming Console UX features: new per-route dashboards, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback), and the cost transparency panel. This ticket consolidates release notes drafting, cross-team launch readiness, stakeholder sequencing, training materials, and the post-launch monitoring plan.
goals: Ship a single, reusable GTM playbook that engineering, design, support, and marketing can follow
Ensure release notes and API change communication are synchronized across SDKs and docs
Prepare customer-facing training (webinar + quickstarts) focused on interpreting dashboards and configuring rollouts
Minimize post-launch incidents by validating SLOs, runbooks, and escalation paths in advance
success_metrics: < 5% spike in latency-related support tickets in first 2 weeks
> 70% of active customers see the new cost breakdown in Console within week 1
Webinar attendance >= 250 and on-demand views >= 750 in 30 days
Release notes opened by 60% of org-admin accounts within 72 hours
launch_steps: Finalize UX copy and screenshots (DES review complete) - target 2026-03-12
Merge console backend PRs and smoke test in staging (ENG) - target 2026-03-18
Coordinate SDK patch notes and version bump (Docs & SDK) - target 2026-03-20
Draft and sign-off release notes + API changelog - target 2026-03-22
Run internal training session for Support and Solutions (CS) - target 2026-03-25
Schedule customer webinar and create on-demand video - target 2026-03-27
Gradual rollout with canary policy: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours with automated rollback guardrails - start 2026-03-30
Monitor SLOs and cost metrics; execute incident playbook if thresholds breached - ongoing after rollout
comms_plan: Internal: Kickoff deck in #console-product (link below) and weekly readout during PM sync
External: Coordinated release email to org admins, in-console banner for 14 days, and webhook to announce-change channel for partners
Release notes: single-source markdown stored in Drive + push to docs site during release window
Escalation: On-call SRE and on-call PM contact info included in release notes and support playbook
training_plan: 60-minute live webinar (recorded) covering dashboards, interpreting cost breakdowns, and setting rollout policies
Hands-on quickstart: 10-minute guided walkthrough to configure a canary rollout and view cost delta
Internal playbook for Support with sample customer Q&A and troubleshooting checklist
One-pager cheat sheet for sales to position feature benefits and limitations
release_notes_draft: Highlights: Per-route latency and token-cost dashboards, new rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback) with safe defaults, and an opt-in cost transparency panel showing per-model and per-route token breakdown. API: new 'rolloutPolicy' field in CreateDeployment v1 and a small extension to Usage API. Backward compatible defaults applied. Known issue: historic cost aggregation for pre-2026-03 data will be approximate for the first 48 hours.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rollout triggers unexpected latency in heavy traffic tenants -> Mitigation: canary limited to 5% with automated latency threshold rollback
Risk: Customers confused by new cost panel numbers -> Mitigation: include clear definitions, examples, and a guided quickstart
Risk: Docs/SDK drift causes integration errors -> Mitigation: freeze SDK swath 48 hours before release and run integration smoke tests
Risk: Support overloaded on day 0 -> Mitigation: temporary ticket triage queue and dedicated CS on-call for 72 hours
rollout_schedule: 2026-03-30 00:00 UTC - start canary (5% of orgs) - monitor for 6 hours
2026-03-30 06:00 UTC - evaluate telemetry; if healthy, expand to 25%
2026-03-30 18:00 UTC - expand to 100% if thresholds OK; otherwise pause and investigate
Rollback guard: latency increase > 20% or error-rate increase > 5% triggers automatic rollback
post_launch_tasks: 72-hour monitoring report (SRE) and summary to leadership
Customer feedback analysis and top-5 change requests backlog grooming
Close loop with marketing on campaign performance and content updates
Update FAQs and add 2-3 clarifying screenshots based on early support trends
